sources.news_title: REPORT: Bessent Likely To Be Named Trump’s “AI Czar”
sources.text:
Semafor reports:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is emerging as a frontrunner for President Donald Trump’s new “AI czar” position, three sources familiar with the matter told Semafor.
Bessent has long played a central role in the Trump administration’s AI policy, and this week he’s already held a critical early dialogue with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
Bessent and He discussed a potential US-China “notification mechanism” to facilitate communication about AI incidents that pose threats to national security, as part of what Bessent said were talks about a formal US-China dialogue on AI.
Read the full article.

sources.news_title: U.S. treasury secretary could take on AI czar role, source tell Reuters
sources.text: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could become President Donald Trump’s new AI czar, a source familiar with the discussions said on Tuesday, as fears grow among lawmakers in Washington about the risks posed by AI technology. Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI and argued that additional regulation is unnecessary. Treasury had no immediate comment on Bessent’s possible new role, which was first reported by Semafor. Trump on Saturday said that he plans to appoint a new artificial intelligence advisor, known as an “AI czar,” and create an “AI force,” though he did not provide details about either initiative or how they would be implemented. Bessent led talks on Sunday with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York ahead of this week’s summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. The talks focused heavily on AI. Bessent told reporters after the talks that Washington had proposed a new AI safety notification mechanism and a new U.S.-China AI dialog, with a particular emphasis on national security concerns. Trump previously tapped Bessent, a former hedge fund manager, to play a lead role in a major revamp of U.S. trade policy, negotiate with Ukraine about critical minerals and temporarily head the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. He also serves as acting commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service, and his Treasury is leading a push to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and other measures. Editing by Cynthia Osterman

Goddard earned degrees from Vassar College and Harvard University. He lives in New York with his wife and three sons.
Goddard is the owner of Goddard Media LLC.
